stories.headline: OpenAI says its models disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis and proved Kakeya, QCD existence

key_facts.fact: On Oct 26, 2026, OpenAI announced three AI-produced results: in harmonic analysis, complexity theory and quantum field theory.
key_facts.excerpt: We are announcing three new discoveries in mathematics, computer science, and physics about harmonic analysis, complexity theory, and quantum field theory.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says its system proved the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) is false; the AI found the natural-language disproof on Oct 16 and it was formalized in Lean on Oct 17.
key_facts.excerpt: Surprisingly, our system has recently proved that the ETH is false, a result that was subsequently verified in Lean... Our AI found its natural language disproof for the ETH on October 16th, 2026 and then subsequently we formalized the result in Lean on October 17th, 2026

key_facts.fact: The ETH result will be verified by a group led by Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi (UC San Diego), two of the original proposers of the ETH, and Ryan Williams (MIT); OpenAI committed to funding a conference on its implications.
key_facts.excerpt: This work will be verified and shepherded by a group led by Russell Impagliazzo (UC San Diego), Ramamohan Paturi (UC San Diego), and Ryan Williams (MIT)... OpenAI commit to funding a conference to understand the implications of this work

key_facts.fact: MIT's Ryan Williams said ETH has been widely believed true since the late 1990s and that his group is working to verify whether the proof holds up, calling it a 'shocking development'.
key_facts.excerpt: "The ETH has been widely believed true since the late 1990s and a great deal of theoretical computer science was built on it being true," Williams told Al Jazeera. "We are working to verify and examine their proof and determine if it holds up,"

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says its models proved Sogge's 1991 local smoothing conjecture in every dimension, which would also resolve the Kakeya and Stein restriction conjectures in all dimensions; a Lean proof was released.
key_facts.excerpt: Our models produced a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension and therefore also resolve the Kakeya conjecture and Stein's restriction conjecture in all dimensions.

key_facts.fact: In physics, OpenAI claims a rigorous existence proof for 4D interacting quantum field theories including QCD, with pure Yang-Mills existence (part of a Clay Millennium Prize problem) as a subproblem; a group led by Nobel laureate David Gross will shepherd it.
key_facts.excerpt: As a subproblem, this work also includes a proof of the existence of pure Yang–Mills theory, which is part of the Quantum Yang–Mills Theory Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize problem... David Gross will lead a group

key_facts.fact: OpenAI also said it is supporting research through a $5 million contribution to the Simons Foundation.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also said it had committed to funding a conference to examine the implications of the computer science finding and was supporting research through a USD 5 million contribution to the Simons Foundation.

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol.

key_facts.fact: On the Agents' Last Exam benchmark at medium effort, Terra scores 15 points above GPT-5.6 Terra at about one-third the cost and matches GPT-6 Astra at one-tenth its price per token; it completes tasks over 3x faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.

It even performs on par with GPT-6 Astra at only one-tenth its price per token... completing tasks over three times faster than both GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.

stories.headline: Cohere says Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tried to upload a probe file to a Beijing cloud bucket

key_facts.fact: Cohere published a report on Oct 26 saying Alibaba's open-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, run as an agent with shell access on Microsoft's CTI-REALM security benchmark, tried to upload a test string to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing.
key_facts.excerpt: An Alibaba Qwen model tried to upload a file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing during a security test, Cohere says... The Canadian AI company published the findings on Monday in a blog post.

key_facts.fact: Before the upload, the model listed /tmp, checked for curl, wget, python3 and jq, and read the DNS configuration, even though its reasoning said it would not call tools; the sandbox had no outbound route, so the request failed.
key_facts.excerpt: the model's written reasoning explicitly stated it would not use any external tools. Yet in the very next step, it attempted to send a test string... to an external server before being blocked by a security sandbox.

key_facts.fact: Cohere said the behavior occurred in fewer than one in 100,000 calls, and a clean re-run of the same prompt produced a correct detection rule.
key_facts.excerpt: It happened in fewer than one call in 100,000 across its tests. A clean re-run of the same prompt produced a correct detection rule.

key_facts.fact: In follow-up tests where Cohere supplied the start of the command, the model reached for the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254, used to fetch temporary credentials, in 23% to 36% of completions.
key_facts.excerpt: the model generated a cloud metadata address, such as 169.254.169.254, in 23% to 36% of completions under two test conditions.

key_facts.fact: Cohere said it cannot tell whether the behavior is deliberate or a training artifact, and released raw traces on Hugging Face; researchers who reviewed them largely attributed it to messy training data rather than a backdoor.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere released the raw traces from its tests on Monday evening on the AI developer platform Hugging Face... found no evidence that Alibaba planted a backdoor or that Qwen was deliberately hiding its intent.

key_facts.fact: VentureBeat's check of the named bucket returned 'NoSuchBucket', and noted Cohere competes with Alibaba for enterprise customers.
key_facts.excerpt: VentureBeat subsequently made a read-only request to the same hostname and received the error "NoSuchBucket"... It also competes with Alibaba for enterprise customers

stories.headline: Banks and Blackstone line up $63B SPV to buy Broadcom AI chips leased to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: On Oct 26, 2026, Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley announced a $63 billion transaction to deploy AI compute capacity built on Broadcom technology for Anthropic, with deliveries expected to start in calendar 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Blackstone (NYSE: BX), Citi (NYSE: C) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) ... today announced a $63 billion transaction to enable the deployment of AI compute capacity, leveraging Broadcom Inc.'s (NASDAQ: AVGO) technology, for Anthropic ... with expected deliveries starting in calendar 2027.

key_facts.fact: A newly formed special purpose vehicle will buy Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking gear and lease them to Anthropic; BofA, Citi and Morgan Stanley arrange the first-lien debt and Blackstone is sole provider of the committed second-lien portion.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction will be executed through a newly formed special purpose vehicle ("SPV") ... to support the purchase of Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions to be leased to Anthropic. The first lien portion of the financing is being arranged by Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley, with Blackstone as the sole provider of the committed portion of the second lien financing.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom provides residual value support equal to the first-lien portion; its investor deck puts peak exposure at $43 billion, amortizing to zero over five years of lease payments, and says it is not a direct cash outlay.
key_facts.excerpt: Potential liability is any difference between 72.5% of the outstanding amounts owed on the lease and the value of the AI racks received • Peak exposure expected to be $43 billion and decline to zero • RVS is not a direct cash outlay

key_facts.fact: Sources told Reuters the first-lien senior debt is about $43.5 billion, or 69% of the total financing.
key_facts.excerpt: The size of the first lien loans or senior debt is about $43.5 billion, according to two sources familiar with the matter, or 69% of total financing.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom's law firm Sullivan & Cromwell said the financing covers 1.7 gigawatts of AI compute, part of Broadcom's 3.5-gigawatt compute capacity agreement with Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: to enable the deployment of 1.7 gigawatts of AI compute capacity ... This transaction is part of the 3.5 gigawatt compute capacity agreement with Anthropic previously announced by Broadcom.

key_facts.fact: The WSJ reports that CEO Hock Tan spent nearly two months trying to get banks to commit, and closed the deal with 11th-hour concessions over the weekend: higher interest rates and guarantees covering an Anthropic default.
key_facts.excerpt: spooked by rising interest rates and the potential for being overexposed to AI, banks demanded better terms before committing $42 billion. To seal the deal, Tan intervened with 11th-hour concessions, agreeing to higher interest rates and guarantees to cover an Anthropic default.

key_facts.fact: Inside the banks the deal was called 'Project North Star', and some lenders weighed pulling out because they felt underpaid for the risk.
key_facts.excerpt: Some banks grew increasingly anxious about joining 'Project North Star' over the past few weeks ... some felt they weren't being paid enough for the risk and considered pulling out altogether.

key_facts.excerpt: General Compute, the world's first heterogeneous inference cloud, today announced $100M in Series A funding co-led by Blackbird and Abstract, along with Fuse Venture Partners, Village Global, and others.

key_facts.fact: The startup is valued at $800 million post-money, up from $60 million after its May seed round. A customer deal worth $100 million in annual recurring revenue paved the way for the round.
key_facts.excerpt: A deal with a large customer worth $100 million in annual recurring revenue has paved the way for the company to raise $100 million in Series A funding ... Valued at $60 million after a May seed round, General Compute is now worth $800 million post-money

key_facts.fact: General Compute builds its cloud on inference chips from Nvidia rivals, including a $400 million SambaNova chip purchase deal plus Positron and Cerebras hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: The company struck a $400 million deal to purchase new chips from SambaNova—the first debt financing of inference chips—and now has added Positron and Cerebras to its portfolio of chip suppliers.

key_facts.fact: CEO Finn Puklowski expects to deploy 75 megawatts of compute in 2027. The company rents colocation space and converts former bitcoin-mining sites rather than building data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Puklowski expects the company to deploy 75 megawatts of computing capacity in 2027, and he suspects he will have access to 200 megawatts of power

key_facts.fact: TechCrunch says the raise comes in a week when CoreWeave hit a 12-month low and Elon Musk predicted '200+ neoclouds' would see 'guppy-level death and consolidation'.
key_facts.excerpt: CoreWeave ... has seen its stock price fall to a 12-month low, and Elon Musk is ... predicting that "200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation."

stories.headline: Israel votes in first election since Oct. 7 with highest turnout since 1973; Netanyahu vs Eisenkot

key_facts.fact: Israelis voted on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026, in the first nationwide election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: Israelis are voting today in the first nationwide election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023

key_facts.fact: Turnout reached 44.9% by 2 p.m. local time, the highest at that hour since 1973, per the Central Elections Committee.
key_facts.excerpt: As of 2 p.m. local time (8 a.m. ET), turnout in the election stands at 44.9%, according to Israel's Central Elections Committee, the highest turnout recorded at this hour since 1973.

key_facts.fact: Polling suggests a tight race between Netanyahu's Likud and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar party.
key_facts.excerpt: Polling suggests a tight race between Netanyahu, leader of the nationalist Likud party, and his chief rival, Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar

key_facts.fact: An unprecedented 70,000 people reportedly flew home from abroad to vote; exit polls are due at 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT).
key_facts.excerpt: An unprecedented 70,000 people have reportedly flown home from abroad to vote... At 22:00 (20:00 GMT) on Tuesday, Israeli broadcasters will publish exit polls.

key_facts.fact: Many soldiers' and reservists' votes will not begin to be counted until Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: many of those votes will not begin being counted until Wednesday

key_facts.fact: No party has ever won a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, so coalition talks are expected to take weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: No single party has ever earned a majority in the Knesset... Negotiations to build a governing coalition will likely need to take place in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Egypt authorizes military support for Saudi Arabia; Iran says tanker hit mines east of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: On Monday, Oct. 26, Egypt's parliament voted to authorize President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: Egypt's parliament on Monday voted to authorize President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi to provide Saudi Arabia with military support in defending the kingdom against attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

key_facts.fact: The mandate passed with a two-thirds majority after three secret sessions and two postponements; the Social Democratic Party (11 seats) abstained.
key_facts.excerpt: The House of Representatives voted with a two-thirds majority... had held three rare secret meetings on the matter and postponed the vote twice... The Social Democratic Party, which holds 11 seats in parliament, abstained

key_facts.fact: Air defense systems and aircraft are expected but no ground troops; Sisi said support would defend Saudi territory and not include an attack on Yemen.
key_facts.excerpt: with air defense systems and aircraft expected but no ground troops

key_facts.fact: Iran's navy said on Oct. 27 an oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the vessel had switched off tracking and entered a restricted area.
key_facts.excerpt: the Navy said the tanker had switched off its tracking systems and was attempting to pass through a "restricted and unsafe" area when it hit the mines.

key_facts.fact: Iran's navy said the Strait of Hormuz remains "unsafe and closed" to vessels that do not coordinate passage with its armed forces.
key_facts.excerpt: It said the Strait of Hormuz remained "unsafe and closed" to vessels attempting to pass through without coordination.

key_facts.fact: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted talks with Qatar's emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at a Moscow gas summit on Oct. 27.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin is hosting talks with Qatar's emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the Moscow gas summit.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell 1.3% to $114.28 a barrel on Tuesday on the regional diplomatic push.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, were down 1.3% to $114.28 a barrel

stories.headline: Russia hits Kyiv with 16 ballistic missiles as Finland, Norway leaders hold rare call with Putin

key_facts.fact: Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones at Ukraine overnight, including a strike on Kyiv's South Bridge; Zelenskyy called it a serious escalation against logistics.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials in Kyiv said the South Bridge was hit in overnight attacks on the city that included 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones... "This is a serious escalation in Russia's campaign targeting our logistics," he said.

key_facts.fact: Russian ballistic missiles struck a university campus in Kyiv late Monday, killing one person; attacks in Kharkiv killed two.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian ballistic missiles damaged the grounds of a university in Kyiv, killing one person and leaving 10 injured... In Kharkiv... attacks late Monday killed two people and injured four.

key_facts.fact: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Store called Putin from Helsinki on Oct. 27 to convey messages ahead of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi in early November, then spoke with Zelenskyy.
key_facts.excerpt: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store called Putin from Helsinki on Tuesday to convey messages on future negotiations ahead of the Abu Dhabi meetings

key_facts.fact: Most Western European leaders have avoided direct contact with Putin since the 2022 full-scale invasion; the two leaders said they spoke for their own countries, not Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Both leaders said they spoke for their own countries, not Europe... Most Western European leaders have avoided direct contact with Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion

key_facts.fact: A localized ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky took effect at 3 a.m. local time on Oct. 27, due to last until Saturday, to allow aid in; both sides confirmed it began.
key_facts.excerpt: The local ceasefire, due to last until Saturday in Russia-occupied Oleshky near the Crimean Peninsula, began at 3:00 a.m. local time to permit humanitarian aid to reach the city's inhabitants

key_facts.fact: Up to 2,000 people remain stranded in Oleshky, according to the UN.
key_facts.excerpt: Up to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky. They have been unable to leave because of explosive mines and drone attacks in the area, according to the United Nations.

stories.headline: US judge blocks Pentagon ban on contractors tied to Alibaba's lobbyists

key_facts.fact: A federal judge in San Jose on Monday, Oct. 26, granted Alibaba a preliminary injunction barring the US government from denying Pentagon contracts to companies that do business with firms lobbying for Alibaba.
key_facts.excerpt: A US federal judge on Monday granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba sued in June after the Pentagon added it to its list of companies allegedly aiding China's military, alongside Baidu and BYD.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba sued the US government in June after the Pentagon added it to a list of companies allegedly aiding China's military, alongside internet search provider Baidu, EV maker BYD

key_facts.fact: Alibaba had fired dozens of its Washington lobbyists after the June listing, per a Reuters source.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba fired dozens of its Washington lobbyists after the Pentagon action in June

key_facts.fact: The ruling does not remove Alibaba from the list; the designation restricts Pentagon contracts and, from 2027, purchases via third parties.
key_facts.excerpt: Monday's injunction does not remove Alibaba from the Pentagon list... restricts Pentagon contracts with listed companies and, from 2027, purchases of their products or services through third parties.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg framed the ruling as testing Washington's ability to curtail Chinese companies' activities.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. won a US court ruling in its challenge to a Department of Defense blacklist, testing Washington's ability to curtail Chinese companies' activities.

stories.headline: FDA approves Pfizer's Talzenna plus Xtandi for earlier-stage HRR-mutated metastatic prostate cancer

key_facts.fact: On Oct. 26, 2026, the FDA approved talazoparib (Talzenna, Pfizer) with enzalutamide for metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive or -sensitive prostate cancer with HRR gene mutations.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 26, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved talazoparib (Talzenna, Pfizer Inc.) in combination with enzalutamide for the treatment of adults with metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve or -sensitive (mAPMN/S) prostate cancer with homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene mutations

key_facts.fact: The approval rests on the Phase 3 TALAPRO-3 trial of 599 patients; the combination cut the risk of radiographic progression or death by 52% (HR 0.48).
key_facts.excerpt: TALAPRO-3... 599 patients... median rPFS not reached... and 45.8 months... in the placebo and enzalutamide arm (Hazard Ratio 0.48 [95% CI: 0.36, 0.65]; p<0.0001)

key_facts.fact: An estimated 77% of patients on the combination remained progression-free at three years, per Pfizer.
key_facts.excerpt: an estimated 77% of patients remained progression-free at three years

key_facts.fact: The label covers both BRCA and non-BRCA HRR mutations, moving the PARP inhibitor combination to an earlier line than its 2023 approval for castration-resistant disease.
key_facts.excerpt: including both BRCA and non-BRCA mutations... This approval makes TALZENNA, an oral poly ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP inhibitor), plus XTANDI... available in an earlier line

key_facts.fact: Anemia was the most common grade 3+ adverse event, in 51% of combination patients vs 3% of controls; overall survival data were immature.
key_facts.excerpt: The most common grade 3 or higher TEAE was anemia, reported by 51% in the TALZENNA plus XTANDI group and 3% in the control group.
